## The failing line

**`bentcut`'s report — and the committed summary's `t34.faces` — depend on `--workers` (C-0242 (7) says they do
not).** In `index.ts:216` the T34-1 phase reads the faces in batches of `want = Math.max(10, 2 * workers)` and adds
every face of every batch it ran to `t34Records`. Their count becomes `t34.faces`, and the same records feed the work
block (`index.ts:244`). The batch overshoots the face that gives the n-th g, so the count includes faces that gave no
draw, and it moves with the batch size.

* CONFIRMED in the tree: at `--workers 4` the bar run gives `T34-1 … over 10000 faces' draws (490 districts)`. The
  committed summary, from the author's `--workers 6` run, has `"faces": 492`. Every other field is identical.
* CONFIRMED in mirror m2: `bench -- bentcut --only t34 --t34 30` gives `(10 districts)` at `--workers 1` and
  `(12 districts)` at `--workers 6`. Under `--only t34` the work block also differs (`districts` 10 vs 12). The g list,
  the mean, the s.e. and the verdict are identical.
* Why the item's test misses it: `entry.test.ts` compares one worker with two, and `max(10, 2w)` is 10 for every w ≤ 5.

This makes the item's committed, numbers-only summary unreproducible from its own command at an honest worker count,
and it overstates the districts the 10 000 draws came from. That is a wrong result on an honest input, and it breaks
the item's stated determinism contract (C-0242 (7); N-45 (a) / (b)). No judged number moves.

**Required change:** make the T34-1 phase independent of the worker count. Either use a fixed batch size, or keep
`t34Records` (and so `t34.faces` and the work block) to the faces up to the one that supplied the n-th g. Pin it with
a test that compares reports at 1 worker and at ≥ 6 workers (or that runs `bentcut()` with `workers` 1 and 6 on an
in-thread runner). Re-run `corepack pnpm bench -- bentcut --workers W --summary` and re-land. `t34.faces` will change
to the count of contributing faces; record that one-time shift in the choices row.
